source.name: Israeli Pop
source.lineage: Tel Aviv commercial song from the 1970s onward, formed when the Ashkenazi-European Shirei Eretz Yisrael tradition was overtaken by Mizrahi cassette culture from the Yemenite and Iraqi neighbourhoods — bouzouki and oud tremolo lines, darbuka doubling a rock kit, Hebrew lyric sung with Arabic-derived melisma, and 100-130 BPM verse-chorus forms.

extras.description: Israeli pop is the mainstream Hebrew-language song style of Tel Aviv radio and the central bus station cassette stalls, decisively reshaped between the 1970s and 1990s as musika mizrahit moved from the margins to the charts. The defining sound pairs a Western rock rhythm section with bouzouki and oud tremolo, darbuka on the backbeat, and vocals that carry Yemenite or Iraqi ornamentation over major-minor or hijaz harmony. It is distinguished from Arab pop by Hebrew text and greater use of Greek-Anatolian bouzouki timbre, and from earlier Israeli folk-song by its dance-oriented rhythm and unashamed Middle Eastern melisma.

source.name: Irish rock
source.lineage: Rock made in Dublin, Belfast and Derry from about 1970, codified by Thin Lizzy's twin-harmony lead guitars and Phil Lynott's narrative singing, Horslips' grafting of jigs and reels onto amplified band instrumentation, and U2's early-1980s delay-drenched arpeggio guitar over open-tuned drone chords — mostly straight 4/4 at 110-150 BPM but frequently borrowing Dorian and Mixolydian modal melody, whistle or pipe countermelodies, and a rhetorical, chest-voice vocal delivery.

extras.description: Alpine yodeling is the pan-Alpine practice of leaping between chest and head register on vocables, developed for calling cattle and communicating across valleys before being formalized into club repertoire and competition in the 19th and 20th centuries. extras.description: Ostrock is the rock repertoire made inside the GDR between the late 1960s and reunification, shaped as much by Amiga's monopoly, state licensing of musicians and airplay quotas as by musical choice. The result is a well-drilled, conservatively engineered hard rock with prominent organ and string-machine, competent but unshowy guitar solos, and German lyrics whose ambiguity was the point — City's Am Fenster and Karat's Über sieben Brücken became standards on both sides of the border. It is distinguished from West German Deutschrock by its state-studio uniformity and metaphorical lyricism, and from Soviet magnitizdat rock by being officially released rather than clandestinely taped.

extras.description: The Paisley Underground formed among Los Angeles clubs in the early 1980s as a reaction against hardcore, reclaiming 1960s folk-rock and psychedelia at a moment when that was unfashionable.
